questions.question: A person walks 3 km east then 4 km north. Why is the distance 7 km but the displacement 5 km?
questions.solution: Distance is a scalar — magnitudes simply add. Displacement is a vector — the two legs combine by the head-to-tail rule, giving √(3²+4²) = 5 km at 53° north of east. Vectors carry direction, so they combine geometrically, not arithmetically.

questions.question: Two forces of 5 N each act on a body and the body stays at rest. How can two nonzero forces 'add to nothing'?
questions.solution: If they act in exactly opposite directions, their vector sum is the NULL vector — zero magnitude, no defined direction. The body is in equilibrium: the forces cancel, not vanish. A null vector is a legitimate vector result, not 'no force exists'.

questions.question: A = 3î + 4ĵ and B = 8î − 6ĵ. Show they are perpendicular using the dot product, and say what the dot product physically measures.
questions.solution: A·B = (3)(8) + (4)(−6) = 24 − 24 = 0 → cosθ = 0 → θ = 90°. The dot product A·B = |A||B|cosθ measures the PROJECTION of one vector along the other — zero projection means perpendicularity. Magnitudes (5 and 10) are irrelevant to the direction test.

questions.question: Why does a force F at angle θ to the horizontal contribute F cosθ to horizontal motion and F sinθ to vertical?
questions.solution: Resolution is projection: the component along a direction is the part of the vector that acts that way — F cosθ along the axis making angle θ with F. The two perpendicular components rebuild the full vector (Pythagoras), so nothing is lost or double-counted. Components let 2D problems become two 1D problems.

questions.question: What does |A×B| represent geometrically, and why does swapping the order flip the result?
questions.solution: |A×B| = |A||B|sinθ is the area of the parallelogram spanned by A and B; its direction is perpendicular to both (right-hand rule). Swapping gives B×A = −(A×B): the magnitude is the same but the normal points the opposite way — the cross product encodes orientation, hence it is anticommutative.
